steps.title: Observe sample composition
steps.instruction: Examine the rock sample and note (1) major mineral phases, (2) domains with heterogeneous composition or structure, and (3) mineral shape‑preferred orientation (SPO) or other foliation indicators.

steps.title: Measure and trim dimensions
steps.instruction: Measure the sample dimensions; if possible trim to keep the intermediate dimension < 5 cm (for ≤160 kV systems) to minimise X‑ray path length and maximise geometric magnification.

steps.title: Mount sample for scanning
steps.instruction: Mount the specimen with its long axis vertical so the X‑ray beam traverses the shortest and intermediate dimensions, using low‑attenuating media (e.g., mounting wax or foam‑padded plastic) and verify stability throughout 360° rotation.

steps.title: Acquire flat‑field references
steps.instruction: Move the mounted sample out of the X‑ray field and acquire bright‑field reference images (sample‑free) for flat‑field correction of all projections.

steps.title: Initialize µXCT system
steps.instruction: Power up the X‑ray source, run the manufacturer‑recommended warm‑up to reach thermal stability, initialise the rotation stage and detector, and confirm all system status indicators show normal operation.

steps.title: Select detector and filters
steps.instruction: Choose a detector: flat‑panel for large samples or high‑energy CCD for higher resolution on smaller fields of view. Then select X‑ray filters appropriate to composition; e.g., 1 mm Al + 1 mm Cu for spinel‑bearing peridotite/pyroxenite to enhance spinel‑silicate contrast and reduce beam‑hardening.

steps.title: Define acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Set rotation step, frame averaging, and rotation range in the acquisition dialog. Use coarse values (larger rotation step, no averaging) for preview scans and finer values for the final scan.

steps.title: Run optional preview scan
steps.instruction: Perform a short feasibility scan with voxel size ≈45–60 µm, rotation step ≈0.4–1°, averaging off. Adjust filters or acquisition parameters as needed to avoid clipping, oversaturation, insufficient contrast, or poor penetration.

steps.title: Perform final high‑resolution scan
steps.instruction: Acquire the full‑resolution dataset using the optimised parameters and filters; save all projections as 16‑bit TIFF files and generate a .log file in the designated data folder.

steps.title: Verify projection count
steps.instruction: Confirm the number of saved TIFF files matches the expected count (e.g., 0.1° step → 3600 projections, 0.2° step → 1800 projections) and that the .log file is present.

steps.title: Launch NRecon and import projections
steps.instruction: Open NRecon, import the TIFF sequence; the software will read the .log file to obtain geometric parameters for Feldkamp cone‑beam reconstruction.

steps.title: Set reconstruction parameters
steps.instruction: In NRecon, define: rotation step (≈ detector‑horizontal‑pixel count guideline, e.g., 0.1–0.2°), frame averaging (use only if needed), rotation range = 360°, and enable correction algorithms (beam‑hardening, ring‑artifact reduction, misalignment compensation, smoothing).

substeps.instruction: Beam‑hardening: draw a transect line, adjust correction % until the silicate matrix baseline is flat.
Ring‑artifact reduction: increase value until concentric rings disappear without over‑correction.
Misalignment compensation: fine‑tune using the preview slice tool until double edges vanish.
Smoothing: apply a Gaussian kernel level 1–3; avoid >4 to preserve phase boundaries.

steps.title: Iteratively optimise reconstruction (preview mode)
steps.instruction: Reconstruct a representative preview slice, adjust one correction parameter at a time (misalignment, beam‑hardening, ring reduction, smoothing), regenerate the preview after each change, and repeat until all artefacts are minimised.

steps.title: Configure output settings
steps.instruction: In the Output tab, set the histogram window to span the full data range, enable “Use ROI” and draw a tight ROI around the sample, select 8‑bit BMP format, and verify the output directory and filename prefix.

steps.title: Run full reconstruction
steps.instruction: Start reconstruction with the optimised parameters; after completion, visually inspect the entire slice stack (e.g., in DataViewer) to confirm consistent quality.

steps.title: Import reconstruction into Avizo
steps.instruction: Launch Avizo, import the slice folder produced by NRecon, exclude any slices containing mounting material, and remove any suffix from the Object name so only the sample identifier remains.

substeps.instruction: Set “Original coordinate units” to the preferred option.
Under Resolution, choose “Voxel Size” and enter the voxel size (e.g., 27 µm = 0.027 mm) ensuring cubic voxels (same X, Y, Z).

steps.title: Save Avizo project
steps.instruction: File → Save Project As, store the .hx file in the sample directory, and in the Save Project Policy dialog select “Minimize project computation” to avoid duplicating large intermediate files.

steps.title: Create filtering workspace
steps.instruction: Add a “Filter Sandbox” operation to the .transformed dataset, hide the “Volume Rendering” module, set the viewer to the XY orientation, and move the Slice Number slider to a representative slice showing the full range of target mineral phases.

steps.title: Define ROI for filter testing
steps.instruction: Switch the cursor to the Arrow tool, draw a blue ROI box that includes interior sample, edge, and surrounding air so beam‑hardening and contrast can be evaluated during filter optimisation.

steps.title: Choose and configure filter
steps.instruction: In the Filter Sandbox Properties, open the Filter dropdown and select either:

substeps.instruction: Median filter – set to XY planes, 3 iterative passes (recommended for geological datasets).
Non‑Local Means – use only for low‑contrast (<10 % gray‑value difference) or noisy data; adjust Spatial and Intensity Standard Deviations as needed.

steps.title: Apply selected filter
steps.instruction: Click Apply to generate a new .filtered dataset, then immediately save the project and record the filter type and kernel settings in the project notes.

steps.title: Determine interactive thresholds
steps.instruction: Attach the “Interactive Thresholding” module to the filtered dataset. Increase the lower threshold slider until the mask retreats from background air/wax (record as Threshold 1). Continue raising the threshold until only the high‑density mineral (e.g., spinel) remains (record as Threshold 2).

steps.title: Configure multi‑thresholding
steps.instruction: Add a “Multi‑Thresholding” module, define three regions: Exterior, Matrix, High‑Density Phase. Input Threshold 1 (e.g., 37) for Exterior‑Rock and Threshold 2 (e.g., 91) for Rock‑HD. The module will label Exterior = 0, Matrix = 1, Spinel = 2.

steps.title: Execute segmentation
steps.instruction: Press the green Apply button; the workflow creates a .labels dataset where each voxel is assigned 0, 1, or 2 according to the thresholds.

steps.title: Extract high‑density phase
steps.instruction: Attach an “Arithmetic” module to the .labels dataset, set the Expression to a==2, Apply, then rename the resulting binary label (e.g., “Spinel”).

steps.title: Run label analysis
steps.instruction: Add a “Label Analysis” module to the Spinel label, set Intensity Image = NO SOURCE, Interpretation = 3D, select “Standard Shape Analysis” and verify that Volume3d, BaryCenter3d, EigenValues, and EigenVectors are included. Apply to generate a Spinel.Label‑Analysis spreadsheet.

steps.title: Visualise phase quality
steps.instruction: Connect a “Volume Rendering” module to the Spinel label, adjust opacity and colour for optimal grain visibility, and rotate the model to confirm that grains are neither merged (under‑segmentation) nor fragmented (over‑segmentation).

steps.title: Optional field‑orientation setup
steps.instruction: If the sample has field orientation data, identify a plane parallel to the ground surface on the rock, draw two opposite horizontal lines (up/down), and a third arrow indicating magnetic North to define a geographic reference plane.

steps.title: Optional resample for coordinate transformation
steps.instruction: Right‑click the green filtered tab, add a “Clipping Plane”, set Plane Definition on and normal to (0, 1, 0) (YZ orientation) so the plane aligns with the notched surface.

steps.title: Optional establish volume positioning
steps.instruction: Open the Transform Editor on the Resampled tab, switch to “Relative Global”, rotate the sample so the notched XZ plane faces upward, align X‑axis with the y‑axis, and place the notched edge near the origin.

steps.title: Optional apply field orientation data
steps.instruction: Enter the measured plunge as a negative rotation about the x‑axis and the trend as a negative rotation about the z‑axis in the Transform Editor; verify alignment with field measurements.

steps.title: Optional complete structural transformation
steps.instruction: In Avizo, set Y (green) = North, X (red) = East, Z (blue) = Up. Compute the required pitch rotation to align the sample’s Z axis 90° from X and input it in the “Relative Local” tab; apply and verify visually.

steps.title: Optional apply transformation to labels
steps.instruction: Copy the transformation matrix from the Transform Editor, paste it onto the Labels tab, then right‑click Labels → Resample Transformed Image (Extended) → Apply.

steps.title: Train machine‑learning classifier
steps.instruction: Open the “ML Threshold Selection System” Python app, click 1 → Load Training Data (CSV files), 2 → Input Expert Thresholds (values from the Interactive Thresholding step), 3 → Input Voxel Sizes, and 5 → Train Model (LightGBM). Optionally verify with Training Visualization.

steps.title: Physically align sample with digital twin
steps.instruction: Place the physical rock in front of the monitor, rotate it until the digital volume matches visible landmarks (saw cuts, fractures, large grains), using the Eigenvector planes as guides.

steps.title: Mark foliation trace on specimen
steps.instruction: With the digital model edge‑on to the White Plane (Eigenvectors 1 & 2), draw a razor‑thin line on the rock surface using a waterproof marker, keeping the head stationary to avoid parallax.

steps.title: Cut oriented slab
steps.instruction: Using a rock saw, cut a ~2.5 cm thick slab parallel to the marked Eigenvector 1‑3 trace; smooth the surface and re‑mark the Eigenvector 1 direction on the fresh face.

steps.title: Export raw shape data
steps.instruction: In Avizo, open the Spinel.Label‑Analysis tab, click the Export Data icon, and save the spreadsheet as a CSV file (e.g., SAMPLE_RawData.csv) in a dedicated folder.

steps.title: Clean and format exported CSV
steps.instruction: Open the CSV, delete the first row containing the internal Avizo object name, ensure the header row contains variable names, and replace any absolute zeros in the three EigenVal columns with a tiny constant (e.g., 0.0000001).

steps.title: Prepare data for Python app
steps.instruction: From the cleaned CSV, retain only the 13 core columns required for tensor calculation: Volume3d (mm³), EigenVal1‑3, and the nine EigenVec components (X, Y, Z for each eigenvector). Save as a standard CSV (e.g., Sample01_Std.csv).

steps.title: Prepare data for TomoFab (training)
steps.instruction: Extract the same 13 columns, rename them according to the TomoFab schema (see Table 2), and save as a tab‑separated file (TSV).

steps.title: Batch prediction and fabric calculation
steps.instruction: In the Python app, click 6 → Load Test Data to select all remaining CSV files, then 7 → Predict Analysis to compute sample‑specific Vmin thresholds, click the Mean Fabric button to calculate the final fabric tensor, and finally 8 → Export/Reports to save the results.

steps.title: Extract oriented billet for thin sections
steps.instruction: Trim the oriented slab into a rectangular billet, ensuring at least one straight edge is parallel to the marked Eigenvector 1 direction; cut a small V‑shaped notch or permanent arrow on that edge to record orientation for later thin‑section work.

steps.title: Alternative orientation for pre‑cut samples
steps.instruction: If the sample cannot be re‑cut, measure the rake (pitch) of the digital Eigenvector 1‑2 trace on an existing flat surface using a protractor, record the angle, and later apply a tensor rotation to align independent validation data (e.g., EBSD) with the XRCT coordinate system.
